exposure: risk factors (septic abortion, extended hospitalization, dilatation and curettage, cesarean wound infection, indwelling catheterization, ICU admission, post abortion, recurrent UTI)
outcome: maternal sepsis caused by K. pneumoniae
antimicrobial resistance profile of K. pneumoniae strains (MDR, XDR, PDR)
cohort: The study included 5613 women suspected of having maternal sepsis in five tertiary hospitals.
finding: The study found a high prevalence of carbapenem-resistant *K. pneumoniae* among mothers with suspected sepsis, identifying several associated risk factors including septic abortion, extended hospitalization, and cesarean wound infection.
mod_finding: Cesarean wound infection was significantly associated with maternal sepsis caused by K. pneumoniae.
